A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same VLSBench research work, with complete main text and Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original leakage measurements in Table 1, alignment experiments in Table 2, VLSBench evaluations in Table 3, and supplementary MMSafetyBench results in Table 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and supplementary evaluations.

M1.justification: The four-stage VLSBench construction pipeline, alignment procedures, and Appendix B.1 training losses are unchanged. Removing 'M:' from the Figure 5 caption does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training data, VLSBench safety categories, existing safety benchmarks, and general-capability tasks. Appendix B.3 retains the same MMSafetyBench scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 2, 3, and 5 retain identical comparator rows, including VLGuard, SPA-VL, textual SFT, textual unlearning, and the same base and API models.

E3.justification: Data subsets, training settings in Table 4, evaluation metrics, and judge-model procedures in Sections 2.2 and 4.1 and Appendices B and F are unchanged.

E4.justification: The VSIL verification analyses, Appendix F judge-model case study, category-level plots in Figure 14, and example responses in Figures 15–17 are identical. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the appendices. For example, Table 3 retains safety rates of 21.43% for GPT-4o and 49.78% for Gemini-1.5-pro.

T1.justification: The VSIL definition and R1/R2 formulas in Section 2.1, together with the unlearning loss formulations in Appendix B.1, are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about visual safety leakage, VLSBench, and the relative suitability of textual and multimodal alignment.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the alignment gap and refusal-versus-warning behavior are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning model coverage, closed-model costs, and the need for more effective alignment solutions.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the advertised code/data URL from https://hxhcreate.github.io/VLSBench/ to https://hxhcreate.github.io/vlsbench.github.io/. Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, and appendix prompt templates remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether resource availability improves.

R1.justification: Section 5, the 68 references, and the positioning relative to existing safety benchmarks and alignment methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Figure 5's caption removes the stray 'M:' before 'Mitigating visual leakage,' and the arXiv version/date stamp updates. The remaining prose, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer project URL causes local reflow of the abstract and introduction on pages 1–2, and the Figure 5 caption has a small textual/layout adjustment. Figure and table displays otherwise remain identical, including all appendix pages.

improvement.justification: The revision consists of a project-URL update, a tiny caption cleanup, and local reflow. Scientific content and all appendix material are unchanged, so the caption correction has negligible paper-level impact. The PDFs provide no evidence that the new URL improves code/data access.
